context_title:
Convert the supplied technical description, file, or Repomix export into
exactly 1 self-contained build prompt directing another language model to build
the complete system from scratch using only that prompt. Return only the prompt,
without an implementation.

Before writing, read the entire input character by character, line by line, from
beginning to end.

The resulting prompt must:

1.  Specify exactly what to construct and how, in explicit, dependency-ordered
    steps from initial setup through complete implementation.
2.  Preserve every nonexcluded input detail, fully specifying functionality,
    architecture, dependencies, configuration, data structures, interfaces,
    workflows, edge cases, and implementation details. Inline all required
    information without referring to or depending on the original description,
    files, repository, or export.
3.  Identify every necessary file and specify its contents and behavior. Require
    delivery of all files with complete, unabridged, production-ready contents
    and every implementation written in full.
4.  Prohibit simplified, mock, placeholder, dummy, simulated, fake, abbreviated,
    or partially implemented content, omitted code, and instructions to finish
    components later.
5.  For reimplementations, never mention the original software’s name. Replace
    name-bearing identifiers with neutral descriptive identifiers, preserving
    their nonexcluded behavior.
6.  Exclude security, rate limiting, billing, payments, subscriptions, limits,
    tests, documentation, and code comments from the system and deliverables.
    These exclusions override all completeness requirements.
7.  Use explicit, strictly technical, objective instructions without
    role-playing, persona framing, personalization, polite filler, or commentary
    about the rewriting process.
8.  I send a single file, and the frontend must always be contained in a single
    index.html file, including all subpages without backend (you dont have to
    deal with it) Before returning the completed prompt, check it against the
    entire input. Restore every omitted nonexcluded detail and eliminate any
    dependence on access to the original material.

entries.answer:
Construct a single-file, client-side video-library dashboard as exactly one production-ready `index.html` file. Do not create any other files, backend, server process, build configuration, package manifest, tests, documentation, code comments, security features, rate limiting, payments, subscriptions, billing, account enforcement, or external runtime dependencies. Deliver the complete unabridged contents of `index.html` only. The application must run by opening the file in a modern desktop browser.

Implement the complete interface with semantic HTML, embedded CSS, and embedded vanilla JavaScript. Use no framework, CDN, external images, remote APIs, web fonts, imported assets, or external files. Use inline SVG icons created specifically for this interface, CSS-generated previews, and browser-native APIs. Do not use placeholder text, dummy controls, incomplete states, TODO markers, fake flows, or partially functional actions. Every visible control must perform the interface behavior described below without a backend.

Use a dark, high-density professional video-workspace visual system. The page must fill the viewport, use an almost-black charcoal background, muted dark panels, thin low-contrast borders, rounded controls, white primary text, gray secondary text, and a cool blue-violet selection accent. Use a responsive layout that works from narrow mobile widths through large desktop widths. Respect reduced-motion preferences. Provide keyboard focus styling, keyboard-operable controls, meaningful labels, dialog focus management, Escape-to-close behavior, and accessible live announcements for state changes.

Create an application shell with these components in dependency order:

1. Create an application state object containing:
   - `activeTab`: one of `renders`, `previews`, or `partial`.
   - `sortOrder`: initially `latest`; support `latest` and `oldest`.
   - `viewMode`: initially `grid`; support `grid` and `row`.
   - `selectMode`: initially false.
   - `selectedIds`: a `Set`.
   - `sidebarOpen`: initially true on desktop and false on compact widths.
   - `queueOpen`: initially false.
   - `surveyOpen`: initially true.
   - `activeDialog`: initially null.
   - `mediaItems`: 15 initial completed-render records.
   - uploaded media records added through file selection or drag-and-drop.

2. Define each media record with `id`, `name`, `status`, `createdAt`, `duration`, `source`, `previewKind`, and `objectUrl`. Set all 15 initial records to `status: "renders"`. Give them distinct neutral title strings, staggered timestamp values, varying durations, and distinct CSS preview styles. Do not use product names, company names, real user names, email addresses, identifiable account data, or source-service URLs. Render the initial tab counters as 15 completed renders, 0 previews, and 0 partial renders. Recalculate every counter whenever records change.

3. Build a fixed top navigation bar:
   - On the left, render a compact sidebar-toggle icon button followed by a neutral abstract geometric wordmark button that returns the main view to the completed-renders tab and clears selection state.
   - Render a single selected navigation destination labeled “My videos,” using a play-shaped icon.
   - On the right, render a non-payment numeric resource badge showing `53`, plus a “Queue” button.
   - Include a visually hidden, multiple-file input restricted to `video/mp4`.
   - Place a full-page drag target behind the content while preserving interaction with normal controls.

4. Build a collapsible left sidebar:
   - Include a collapse button and close it when the page overlay is clicked on compact screens.
   - Provide navigation buttons labeled “New,” “Account,” “Apps,” and “Bloom,” with “New” carrying a compact “New” badge.
   - Make “New” trigger the file chooser.
   - Make “Account,” “Apps,” and “Bloom” update an accessible current-view announcement and selected sidebar styling without leaving the page.
   - At the bottom, create a profile button with a neutral one-letter circular avatar, a generic workspace email string, and a compact “Free” status. Clicking it opens a small menu with a sign-out-style action that clears local UI selections and closes overlays.

5. Build the primary library page:
   - At the upper left, show an upload call-to-action. On desktop, show “Drag and drop a video to start,” then “or,” then a “Browse files” button. On compact widths, replace the first two lines with “Start a new file.” The browse button opens the MP4 file chooser.
   - Add three tabs: “Renders,” “Previews,” and “Partial renders.” Each tab includes its live count and uses selected styling for the active tab.
   - Add a “Select” toggle. When enabled, show the batch toolbar and selection checkboxes or selection overlays on every visible media item.
   - Add “Sort by” with a custom accessible menu. The initial visible option is “Latest”; the alternate option is “Oldest.” Sorting must reorder the rendered items by `createdAt`.
   - Add two compact view-toggle buttons labeled “row” and “grid,” with grid selected initially.
   - In grid mode, render visible records in a responsive three-column masonry-style layout on wide screens, two columns on medium screens, and one column on narrow screens. Keep vertical gaps consistent and vary tile aspect ratios.
   - In row mode, render the same records as full-width rows containing preview artwork, title, duration, status, creation time, and selection affordance.

6. Implement visible media tiles:
   - Each tile is a button with an accessible label derived from its record name and status.
   - Initial records must have visually distinctive, locally generated CSS artwork: use layered gradients, abstract blobs, overlays, grain-like patterns made from CSS, and a translucent play icon. Do not load images.
   - Uploaded MP4 files must create a record from the actual selected `File`, use `URL.createObjectURL`, display a playable muted `<video>` preview inside the tile, and extract duration after metadata loads.
   - Clicking a tile outside selection mode opens a media-inspection dialog showing the actual video preview where available; generated initial artwork opens an artwork detail panel with name, duration, status, and creation time.
   - Clicking a tile in selection mode toggles its selected state without opening the inspection dialog.
   - Selected tiles must have a visible accent border and selected overlay.

7. Build the batch toolbar, visible only when selection mode is enabled:
   - Include “Select all,” “Download,” “Share,” and “Delete.”
   - “Select all” toggles between selecting all currently visible records and clearing them.
   - “Download” must download every selected uploaded file through browser-created object URLs. For initial records, generate and download a small valid locally created text manifest containing that item’s neutral metadata; do not pretend it is a video file.
   - “Share” opens a confirmation dialog stating that sharing a result makes it publicly accessible and that anyone with the link can view it. The dialog has a “Confirm & share” button. Confirmation must create an in-page share result dialog containing a locally generated fragment identifier link based on the selected record IDs, copy it through `navigator.clipboard` when available, and provide a fallback text-selection method.
   - “Delete” opens a confirmation dialog titled “Remove from Recents,” stating that the selected batch will be removed from Recents and all its output files deleted. Provide “Cancel” and “Remove.” Confirming removes selected records from state, revokes relevant object URLs, exits selection mode if no records remain, and announces the result.

8. Implement video intake and validation:
   - Accept files only when the browser reports `video/mp4` or the filename ends in `.mp4`, case-insensitively.
   - For every rejected file, open an “Unsupported file type” dialog explaining that this file type is not supported in the web application and that the user should upload an MP4 or use a desktop application. Use only neutral wording; do not name any original product or service.
   - On metadata load, reject videos that have fewer than five frames when a frame rate can be inferred, or that have invalid/zero duration, with the exact visible heading “Sorry, we can’t enhance that video.” and explanatory text “Try uploading one with at least 5 frames.”
   - Reject videos whose intrinsic width or height exceeds 3840 or 2160 respectively, using the same visible heading and explanatory text “Try uploading one below 4k resolution.”
   - Valid uploads enter the `previews` state while metadata is loading, then move to `renders` once their preview is available. Update counters and render the new card without reloading the page.
   - Support file-picker selection, drag enter, drag leave, drag over, and drop. While a valid drag is over the application, visibly highlight the drop target. Process every dropped file.

9. Implement the queue:
   - The Queue button toggles a right-side queue drawer. Show uploaded items that are currently in `previews`, their filenames, progress indicators based on metadata readiness, and an empty-state message when there are none.
   - The drawer must close through its close button, Escape, and compact-screen overlay click.

10. Implement the onboarding survey dialog:
    - Open it initially as a centered modal with a softly blurred dark backdrop and layered blue and warm-orange gradient blobs.
    - Show the heading “Welcome to the workspace!” followed by “Let’s tailor it for your work.”
    - Show the prompt “Which of the following best describes you?”
    - Provide radio choices: “Hobbyist / AI Enthusiast,” “Content Creator (YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, X),” “Filmmaker / Videographer / Editor,” “VFX / 3D / Motion Graphics artist,” “Marketing creative / Brand / Agency,” “Producer / Creative Director / Executive,” and “Something else.”
    - Selecting “Something else” must reveal an editable text field. The Continue button remains disabled until a standard option is selected or that text field contains non-whitespace content.
    - Include “Skip for now.” Skip closes the dialog and stores no preference. Continue closes the dialog and displays a concise local toast confirming that the preference was saved for the current page session.
    - Include a two-segment progress indicator with the first segment active.

11. Implement the remaining dialogs:
    - Every dialog needs an accessible title, close button where appropriate, proper modal behavior, focus trap, and a backdrop click rule that closes non-destructive dialogs but not destructive confirmation dialogs.
    - The cancellation confirmation dialog has title “Confirmation,” body text “Are you sure you wish to cancel?”, and buttons “Keep plan” and “Cancel plan.” “Keep plan” closes without changes. “Cancel plan” clears the generic plan-status display and shows a temporary toast.
    - Include an email sign-in modal with heading “Start maximizing quality,” an Email input, an agreement sentence with a locally inert “End User License Agreement” link, an “or continue with” divider, and a “Google” button. Form submission must validate that the email field is non-empty and syntactically email-like, then close the modal and update only the visible generic profile email for the current page session.
    - Make the generic profile menu expose the sign-in modal when no email is present.

12. Create a toast system:
    - Position temporary non-blocking status messages in the lower-right corner on desktop and near the lower edge on mobile.
    - Use it for selection changes, uploads, deletions, sorting, view changes, survey completion, queue actions, cancellation, and sharing completion.
    - Support multiple stacked toasts and automatic dismissal.

13. Finish all visual behavior:
    - Use CSS variables for the complete palette, spacing scale, radius scale, shadows, transitions, and breakpoint behavior.
    - Make the layout avoid horizontal overflow.
    - Preserve a toolbar at the top of the content area while scrolling.
    - Use a full-height scrollable media area.
    - Ensure every state change updates the DOM from the central state object rather than leaving stale counters, selection state, modal content, or object URLs.
    - Clean up object URLs when uploaded records are removed or when the page unloads.
    - Do not mention, import, reference, imitate by name, or depend on any original product, company, repository, application, user account, remote endpoint, or source artifact.

entries.answer:
Kész, a build-promptot frissítettem: kivettem minden desktop-specifikus dolgot (desktop drag-and-drop terület, "váltson desktop appra" fallback szöveg, három oszlopos desktop grid, egér-hover feltételek), és a célt kifejezetten iOS Safari / iOS home-screen web-app futtatásra állítottam. A megfelelő módosítások:

- Viewport és biztonsági terület: `viewport-fit=cover`, `env(safe-area-inset-*)` a felső sávra, alsó eszköztárra és a képernyőszélhez érő panelekre.
- Fájlbevitel csak natív iOS fájl-/fotópicker-en keresztül, nincs asztali drag-and-drop zóna.
- Video preview elemek `playsinline` attribútummal, hogy iOS ne kényszerítsen teljes képernyős lejátszást.
- A grid egy oszlopos iPhone-szélességeken, két oszlopos iPad-osztályú szélességtől.
- Sidebar és sor-menü (Sort by) most off-canvas panel, illetve bottom sheet, ahogy egy natív iOS felületen elvárt.
- „Share” gomb natív iOS share sheet-et hív a Web Share API-n keresztül, clipboard/fallback csak ha az nem elérhető.
- Az „Unsupported file type” dialógusból kivettem minden desktop-app utalást, semleges szövegre cserélve.
- Tap targetek minimum 44×44 pont, swipe gesztusok a sidebar és queue panel bezárásához.

A teljes, frissített promptot egy külön fájlban ([build-prompt-ios.md]) hoztam létre, hogy egy másik nyelvi modell közvetlenül ez alapján építhesse fel a rendszert egyetlen `index.html` fájlként.
